title: New Hope for Patients: NHS Approves Life-Extending Breast Cancer Drug
subtitle: After years of campaigning, a vital treatment for incurable breast cancer is finally available to thousands of women in England.

summary.en: Thousands of women in England with advanced breast cancer will now receive the drug Enhertu through the NHS. This decision follows a successful price agreement between the government and the drug's manufacturers. Previously, the treatment was rejected because it was considered too expensive. Clinical trials show the drug helps patients live longer compared to standard chemotherapy. Health officials and charities have welcomed the news as a major victory for patients.
summary.zh: 英格蘭數以千計的晚期乳癌女性現在將能透過 NHS 獲得 Enhertu 藥物。這項決定是在政府與藥廠達成價格協議後所做出的。先前該治療因被認為過於昂貴而遭拒。臨床試驗顯示，與標準化學治療相比，該藥物能幫助病患延長壽命。衛生官員與慈善機構皆對此消息表示歡迎，認為這是病患的一大勝利。

paragraphs.en: Thousands of women in England living with incurable breast cancer have received life-changing news. Starting this week, the National Health Service (NHS) will provide a drug called Enhertu to patients with a specific type of advanced breast cancer known as HER2-low. This decision comes after a long period of negotiation between the government and the drug’s makers, AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo.
paragraphs.zh: 數以千計居住在英格蘭、患有無法治癒乳癌的女性迎來了改變生命的重大消息。從本週開始，英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）將為患有特定類型晚期乳癌（稱為 HER2 低表現型）的病患提供一種名為 Enhertu 的藥物。這項決定是在政府與該藥物製造商阿斯特捷利康（AstraZeneca）及第一三共（Daiichi Sankyo）進行長期協商後所達成的。

paragraphs.en: The approval marks a significant turning point for about 1,000 women each year who will now be eligible for this treatment. According to The Guardian, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) — an organization that advises the NHS on which medicines offer good value for money — had previously rejected the drug in July 2024. At that time, officials felt the cost was too high to justify. However, after two years of intense campaigning by patients, cancer specialists, and charities like Breast Cancer Now, a new agreement has been reached.
paragraphs.zh: 這項核准對於每年約一千名現在有資格接受此治療的女性來說，是一個重要的轉捩點。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，負責建議 NHS 哪些藥物具備成本效益的國家健康與照顧卓越研究院（Nice），曾在二零二四年七月拒絕了這款藥物。當時官員認為其價格過高，不符合成本效益。然而，經過病患、癌症專家以及如「乳癌現在」（Breast Cancer Now）等慈善機構長達兩年的積極奔走，雙方終於達成新協議。

paragraphs.en: This outcome is the result of what officials call a "commercial solution." The government recently changed its rules to allow the NHS to spend up to £35,000 per patient each year, an increase from the previous limit of £30,000. While it is not fully clear if the pharmaceutical companies lowered their prices, this change in policy allowed the NHS to finally approve the drug for routine use. The Guardian reports that health ministers worked behind the scenes for a long time to make this happen, aiming to bring England in line with Scotland and 27 other European countries that already provide the treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 此結果是官員所謂「商業解決方案」的成果。政府近期修改規定，允許 NHS 每年為每位病患支付最高三萬五千英鎊的費用，高於先前三萬英鎊的上限。雖然目前尚不清楚製藥公司是否調降了價格，但這項政策的改變使 NHS 最終能核准該藥物進行常規使用。《衛報》指出，衛生部長們在幕後進行了長時間的努力，旨在讓英格蘭與蘇格蘭及其他二十七個已經提供此治療的歐洲國家看齊。

paragraphs.en: For many patients, this drug offers something truly precious: more time. Clinical trials have shown that Enhertu is very effective for those whose cancer has continued to grow after other treatments. The data indicates that the drug can help patients live longer and delay the progression of their disease. While standard chemotherapy is a common treatment, Enhertu acts as a targeted therapy, meaning it delivers medicine directly to the cancer cells. According to The Guardian, the median survival time for those using the drug was 23.4 months, compared to 16.8 months for those who did not receive it.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多病患而言，這款藥物提供了真正珍貴的東西：更多的時間。臨床試驗顯示，對於在接受其他治療後癌症仍持續惡化的病患，Enhertu 非常有效。數據顯示，該藥物能協助病患延長壽命並延緩疾病惡化。雖然標準化學治療是常見的治療方式，但 Enhertu 屬於標靶治療，意即它能將藥物直接送達癌細胞。根據《衛報》，使用該藥物的病患中位存活期為二十三點四個月，而未接受該藥物的病患則為十六點八個月。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Anne Rigg, a consultant medical oncologist and a national advisor for the NHS, described the news as "hugely positive" for women with secondary breast cancer. Similarly, Claire Rowney, the chief executive of Breast Cancer Now, called the announcement a "milestone victory." She noted that this decision will give thousands of people the opportunity to spend more time with their loved ones, which is a sentiment shared by many in the medical community.
paragraphs.zh: NHS 顧問級腫瘤內科醫師安妮·瑞格（Anne Rigg）博士形容這項消息對患有繼發性乳癌的女性來說是「極為正面的」。同樣地，「乳癌現在」執行長克萊兒·羅尼（Claire Rowney）稱此公告為「里程碑式的勝利」。她指出，這項決定將讓數千人有機會與摯愛共度更多時光，這也是醫學界許多人的共同心聲。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement, the journey to this point was not easy. The drug’s makers had previously refused to lower their prices, which made negotiations difficult for the government. However, the persistence of campaigners kept the issue in the public eye. Yvette Cooper, the health secretary, stated that the recommendation means NHS patients will finally be able to benefit from a treatment that can be life-changing. She also noted that the success of these negotiations is a tribute to the hard work of those who fought for access to the medication.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管令人振奮，但走到這一步並不容易。該藥物的製造商先前拒絕降價，這使得政府的談判過程相當艱難。然而，倡議者的堅持讓此議題持續受到大眾關注。衛生大臣伊薇特·庫柏（Yvette Cooper）表示，這項建議意味著 NHS 病患終於能受惠於這種足以改變生命的治療。她也提到，談判的成功歸功於那些為爭取藥物使用權而努力奮鬥的人們。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the impact of this decision is expected to spread beyond England. Ministers in Wales and Northern Ireland are likely to follow the recommendation from Nice, which would make the drug available to even more patients across the UK. This development is a clear example of how public pressure and government negotiation can work together to improve healthcare access. For the women who have been waiting for this moment, the approval of Enhertu represents a major step forward in the fight against advanced breast cancer, offering both hope and a better quality of life.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，這項決定的影響預計將擴及英格蘭以外的地區。威爾斯與北愛爾蘭的部長們很可能會遵循國家健康與照顧卓越研究院的建議，這將使英國各地有更多病患能取得該藥物。此發展清楚展現了公眾壓力與政府談判如何共同運作，以改善醫療資源的可近性。對於引頸期盼這一刻的女性而言，Enhertu 的核准代表著對抗晚期乳癌的一大進展，不僅帶來了希望，也提升了生活品質。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To show or prove that something is reasonable or necessary.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處用於說明價格高昂的合理性。文中：At that time, officials felt the cost was too high to justify.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be in agreement with or similar to something else.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述對齊，此處指政策與其他國家同步。文中：aiming to bring England in line with Scotland and 27 other European countries that already provide the treatment.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Working secretly or without public attention.
keyTerms.noteZh: 指不公開的協商過程。文中：The Guardian reports that health ministers worked behind the scenes for a long time to make this happen, aiming to bring England in line with Scotland and 27 other European countries that already provide the treatment.

keyTerms.definitionEn: An act, statement, or gift that is intended to show gratitude, respect, or admiration.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 致敬、頌詞、證明（某人的努力）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處並非指「貢品」，而是指成果歸功於某人的努力。文中：She also noted that the success of these negotiations is a tribute to the hard work of those who fought for access to the medication.

previousArticles.title: New Hope for Breast Cancer Patients as NHS Approves Life-Extending Drug
previousArticles.summaryEn: Patients in England with a specific type of incurable breast cancer can now receive the drug Enhertu through the NHS. The decision follows two years of intense campaigning after the drug was previously rejected for being too expensive. Clinical trials show that the treatment can extend life by several months for those with HER2-low breast cancer. While charities celebrate the news, they also highlight the sadness of those who did not live to see this change. The government and drug companies reached a new agreement to make the medicine available to about 1,000 women each year.

quiz.question: What specific change allowed the NHS to finally approve Enhertu for routine use?

options.A: The drug manufacturers agreed to lower their prices significantly.
options.B: The government increased the maximum spending limit per patient.
options.C: The Nice organization decided the drug was more effective than chemotherapy.
options.D: The health secretary overruled the decision made by the Nice organization.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，政府修改了規則，將每位病患每年的藥費上限從 30,000 英鎊提高至 35,000 英鎊，這項政策變更使得 NHS 得以批准該藥物。選項 A 錯誤，因為文中提到並不清楚藥廠是否真的調降了價格。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提及 Nice 改變了對藥物療效的評估。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到的是透過協商達成協議，並非健康大臣單方面推翻決定。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why did the approval of Enhertu take so long in England compared to other countries?

options.A: The drug was not proven to be effective in clinical trials until late 2024.
options.B: The NHS lacked the necessary medical infrastructure to administer targeted therapy.
options.C: There was a conflict between the cost of the drug and the NHS's budget guidelines.
options.D: Patients and charities were initially opposed to the use of such expensive drugs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第二段提到 Nice 曾於 2024 年 7 月拒絕該藥物，原因是官員認為其成本過高，無法證明其價值（value for money）。第三段進一步說明，直到政府調整了每位病患的預算上限，才解決了這個財務上的僵局。這顯示延遲的主要原因是藥物價格與 NHS 預算限制之間的衝突。選項 A、B 與 D 皆與文中事實不符，文中並未提到缺乏設備或病患反對，且臨床數據早已存在。

quiz.question: In the context of the article, what does the word 'milestone' mean in the phrase 'a milestone victory'?

options.A: A physical marker used to show the distance of a journey.
options.B: A minor achievement that happens during daily routine tasks.
options.C: A significant event that marks a major change or stage in progress.
options.D: A financial payment made to reward successful campaigners.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在此語境下，「milestone」是指在長期抗爭或計畫中，一個具有重要意義的轉折點或重大成就。文中引用 Claire Rowney 的話，將此藥物的批准視為一個重要的勝利，代表抗爭過程中的重大進展。選項 A 是該字的字面意思（里程碑），在此不適用。選項 B 與 D 皆與文中表達的「重大勝利」之意完全相反或無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: To explain the medical benefits of chemotherapy compared to targeted therapy.
options.B: To criticize the pharmaceutical companies for their high pricing strategies.
options.C: To describe how the NHS is changing its internal management structure.
options.D: To highlight how public advocacy and negotiation led to the approval of a life-saving drug.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文的核心在於報導 Enhertu 藥物在英國獲准使用的過程，強調這是病患、慈善機構與政府經過長期協商與抗爭後的成果，並提及這對病患帶來的正面影響。選項 A 只是文章中的背景資訊，非主旨。選項 B 雖然有提到協商困難，但並非文章重點。選項 C 偏離主題，文章未探討 NHS 的整體管理架構變更。
